When I finish playing the first fallout game I love it and I said to myself that this sequel cannot surpass the first one. I was wrong in so many levels.
It picks up right after Fallout 1 and there are many reference to fallout 1 so I recommend playing the first before heading to the second.Fantastic the plot, should I say is better than the first...well is really hard to say because they're both great! In my opinion I slightly sided with the first game plot because of sentimental value moments but the second just nail right in the park with interesting characters, settings, the jokes oh my god the jokes are better than ever because there are some moments that I smile for those humorous wacky moments. The new enemies are interesting like the enclave (I havn't played fallout 3 before this review) sadly I was a slight dissapointment of not much shown on the brotherhood of steel just only a mention on their OPs and I like them in the first game but I understand they want the most focus on the enclaves.
Your partners have a combat control which is awesome that you can put some orders into your team and they do better in combat but it does not mean their AI is better oh no just slightly, the rest the AI of your team can be walking targets at times. Side missions are better than ever especially the many new added towns they put that you can do a lot in their for many hours. I spend countless of hours just to complete the side-missions which are just awesome to complete because each important side missions adds personality of the towns and it will eventually effect the ending depends of actions you take.
I really starting to love the fallout franchise just because of the towns I visit and the different atmosphere the citizens treated you or to others and it adds different layers of problems and situations that can effect other towns as well if you don't take care of the problem. You can be the savior of many towns saying your name like a hero or you can be a complete bully to everyone and doesn't give a dang about anyone and just want money, booze and sex. Each reputation to each of the town you did effects the endings and there are multiple once and even some funny shock once that you can actual impregnate someone and that child will be "this character." Depends on whom you impregnate though is very limit and I wish they put more on that including when choosing a female. I was playing a female and a slave trader wants me to be in bed if I did and got the ending that I have a child and that child will do this I would laugh but instead I didn't and just pop his head by the end of my barrel.
Now there are some minor annoyance when doing specific actions and that is when following some direction to someone only that you the player playing the game for the first time just follows direction. When doing that task you actually miss one conversation to this specific NPC or doing this specific task and thus either lose that oppurtunity to get it back (unless reset a point of the game) and have to either do it the hard way or just lose an event that you wish to explore. I know the game can be specific on their actions toward some events but man can it backfire sometimes to very important events that you either wish you don't miss or don't want to tackle. Like extra experience or easier access to a certain level with ease.
I'm really surprise Interplay is really open and creative with this game back in the late 90s! I will say atleast when playing a female there are hinted of homosexuality which you can actually sleep with other females (don't know males but I'm betting yes). The jokes as I mention again is up high because it tackles some interesting topics that back then videogames had to censor it but this one is like an infant state of Southpark, poking fun of many topics in real life we tackle such as; scientology, American politics, race dispute and drug war. I am so happy they made it so professional about their jokes and not over the top in your face though some you might catch up where are they putting but it isn't enough to make it "controversy" to start yet another arguement. There just many easter eggs, references on different levels of media that I tried google up where are all these little sweet bits come from.
There are many improvements within the game but how about the combat and trading system? Well the combat feels the same as before though I still which I get an extra AP two get two shots instead of only one and not have to wait for a perk but other than that they added some new perks along the way. The trading system they finally fix that issue I had with the cap collecting where you have to press one by one, now you have to hold it and it will raise the caps level faster the longer you hold though to be honest is not exactly what I want I still prefer that wishful thinking where you can change the digit of the number of caps to save even more time but eh is atleast a slightly better.
The bugs I notice they have a bit more than fallout 1 if I'm right? Like some scenarios it won't activated, sometimes my partners even walk through walls or out of the border which I laugh a couple times when Vic just casually walking through an impenetrable base and he walk in the fence and building with no problem. The biggest complaint I should add of the bugs is script errors and even scenes missing! Like don't worry if at some parts you say to yourself "shouldn't it be here or shouldn't the person say something else?" Well that's script error and some scenes missing some bug reasons some developer time constraint and that's kind a sad. Because there are some interesting areas I really want to explore or complete like
Thankfully I heard there are some patches that fix some problems and even improve a better experience to the player even more. The only personal issue I will warn you is once again be careful on running this game on win 10 (and Idk win 7) because it does work and I finish the game but in some areas my fps runs slow like walking in mollasses. I don't know if there is a fix on it or not so please be warn not to break your keyboard if it slows down, just make multiple saves, reset on one point and it will go away for now is not a constant nuisance since is only on some section of a town but it gets frustrating later on if it keeps doing that.
In conclussion I'll give a 9/10 the best sequel of its time and even still to this day, it really does age well to look back and enjoy this masterpiece collection to play again or start a new.

Time to write a review! ( I don't do many but some games warrant them)
This game reminds me alot of Nosgoth, Kingdoms Rise, Panzar, Forge ( had hopes for that one..) which if you enjoyed them games is a good thing however it its an emerging market and so the player base is small having many games end up shutting down due to lack of players.. anyway now on to this one :)
Pros:
+ Graphics are good running on the U4 engine and i have to say optimization is pretty good for and Early Access Game (although i have a pretty good pc - so may vary) however the devs are focusing on optimization as you will see if you read the reviews.
+ Combat - The combat is fluid and easy to get a hold of with a small tutorial at the start (seemed a little rushed but got you the basics)

Cons:
- Small number of classes - but the ones that are out are well polished and fun (so as it is early access ill let them off)
- small number of maps - same as above
- Small player base - again with this being a new market there isnt much hype for games like these & this developer cant afford to promote it just yet, that being said the community that is playing it can be found on discord - active bunch havent shut up since i joined..( the devs are also in there which means you can get ideas across instantly )

Overall if this game keeps going the way they are + advertises it alot more it could be extremely successful,

Now before I say anything else, I would HIGHLY, HIGHLY reccomend getting The Gentlemen of the Row mod for this game. Why? Because other than fixing countless (gamebreaking) bugs, it adds a ton of new content while staying true to the original game. While I can play perfectly fine without it, a lot of other people might not be able to since this is an infamous port full of game-breaking things.
Anyway besides all the technical torment you might have to go through trying to get this game to work, I can tell you it will be worth it especially if you've never played this game before. This game has such interesting gangs with interesting and villanous leaders of them that you will actually feel invested in taking them down and taking hoods for your own. My personal favorite would have to be The Sons of Samedi.
The city of Stilwater is big and is home to so many activities and things to do and explore. There are also easter eggs for those who like the sort and an entire secret mission at the end which clears a lot of things up if you played Saints Row 1. Unlike its sequels it has so much more content even without The Gentlemen of the Row mod such as different brands of stores that are completely missing from 3 and 4, a LOT more activities than 3 and 4, and practically trumping them in comparison. So much so if they continued the formula they had from 2 into its sequels then it would be a massive competitor for something like the GTA series.
If you're considering this game, then I would definitely reccomend this. If you have a friend you can even do co-op together. Multiplayer is also an aspect unlike the other games although it is a little tricky to get working and I've never tried it since I'm scared of completely breaking an already massively unstable port. While its sequels 3 and 4 are awesome games in their own right, if you put them in comparison to this then 2 steamrolls over them with so much more content and in my opinion a much better story and polished world.
In short, get this game you won't be disappointed (if you can get it working of course).

Neushwanstein is one of the most famous castles in Europe, and the inspiration of Disney's Cinderella castle.  It was commissioned to be built by Ludwig II of Bavaria in 1869 and has been open to the public since 1886.  The game takes place in this historical setting with a couple of conspiracy theories thrown in to liven up the plot.
Storyline: Sarah Hamilton of Fact and Fancy (newspaper) stalled in her investigation of a credit fraud scam is sent to Neuschwanstein to investigate rumors about unusual amounts of debris being generated in the refurbishment of the Neushwanstein.  Once there, she meets the resident historian/criminologist Dr. Alder and the castellan Beatrix von Lohen.  Together with Dr. Alder, Sarah uncovers what has been happening during the refurbishment and runs across an ancient mystery.
First of all, I am very impressed by the historical accuracy of Neuschwanstein, King Ludwig II of Bavaria and the authenticity of the castle's interior scenes presented in this game; so few games even try for accuracy when basing their story lines on real places or eras.  The game includes factoids about King Ludwig II and Neuschwanstein, mostly in the form of Dr. Alder's notes and occassional commentary.  Big thumbs up here for accurate information!
However, do not let the educational aspect put one off.  The game play is both easy and challenging at the same time.
How can this be? One is probably asking.   Answer: Easy to follow and fast paced storyline with challenging puzzles.
Gameplay: A nicely blended combination of point and click elements, hidden object scenes and puzzles in a linear story which occurs over six days.  There is a very useful and needed for a few locations fast travel map.   In casual mode, the map shows the places where an action is still required or some clue needs to be found.  No penalties for hints or skips.  Achievements for this game can be earned in a single play through and are for the most part story related.  Nothing is timed.  Three game modes but I suggest Casual play for the little sparkles for two reasons.  1) It is much easier to find the puzzle locations, HO scenes, items, and clues since some are quite small and seem almost hidden.  2) No achievement for Hard mode.  There is a bonus chapter (day 6) which is a mystery all by itself and in some ways ties up the loose ends found in the main story line.
Some special features: The player gets to use their cellphone for emails and as a camera, a UV light, fingerprint powder, and night vision goggles.  The cell phone also holds various folders: one for Sarah’s notes, Dr. Alder’s notes, and King Ludwig’s diary pages.  Plus there is a task folder.  Reading the notes, emails, diary pages prompts the game forward to the next set of tasks.
Hidden Object scenes: Found in logical places like drawers and wall recesses or when looking inside of something.  The HO scenes blend into the gameplay without standing out and the stuff found in the scene is what one would expect to find in that location.  Basically no contrived or ‘just because’ HO scenes.   No find clue is unfairly hidden, but they do blend well into the scene so some are quite tough to find even though they are in plain sight.  There are also interactive clues so look closely for the cursor change.  Some of these finds are quite small, and once again not unfairly hidden and in plain sight.  Some find clues are a bit unusual like cube is a dice die.  So feel no shame in using that Hint button especially when looking for some of the interactive pieces.  NOTE: Late in the game the UV light needs to be used to find some interactive clues. The player is generally prompted by the game when the camera, email, UV light or night vision goggles are needed.

Puzzles: Healthy brain work out challenges and found on locks, computer, and equipment usually.  Logic and maze types mostly: 1) Locks – get the correct combination within X amount of moves.  2)Computer hacking puzzles – free flow type where the players needs to connect the same colors in a continuous “line”.  These are quite a challenge because the grid is not square and each puzzle has three levels. 3) Lock picking – use the lock pick to open the lock in X amount of moves. 4) Connect wires across a moveable tile grid. 5) Skipping/jumping stones – eliminate stones from playing field by jumping over them until only the DESIGNATED STONE is left in the CENTER.  Tough but doable.  6) Rotating sliders.  7) Matching.
Gameplay is about 5-6 hours and well worth the price for many reasons from a built-in history lesson to a great storyline to challenging HO scenes to brain twister puzzles.

You play the role of a Journalist employed by a mystery employer out to find out what is going on at the Neuschwanstein Castle where some unconventional renovations are going on.

This is overall a good enough game, but it also does have a decent enough amounts of faults.  While overall I'm giving it a recommended because the good outweighs the bad, I'd advise to wait on buying for there to be some actual guides out there because this game sorely needs a guide.
Pros:
+NIce visuals.  The style is very good and makes everything look really nice and prevents it from suffering from some of the issues that can exist in the genre.
+Pretty good story.  It's a nice mystery with a logical premise and doesn't rely heavily on the supernatural which does make for a refreshing change of pace.
+Good characters.  The characterization is pretty solid and the characters are reasonably interesting.
+I loved the elements of the camera, UV light and night vision goggles.  It was neat to be able to take a pic of something and use it for a puzzle later or the character would send it to someone and get an email back later about what the object was.
Cons
-The hint system is really not too good.  Hints recharge fast, and that's awesome, but the issue is that about the most direction you'll get is what location to go to, but when you get to that location you have to figure out what to do and if you're stuck it becomes click around everywhere trying to find something new.  If you are playing on easy at least you get some direction with blinking on items you can pick up and interact with, but I also found some didn't blink and it still led to some pixel hunting and guesswork.
-Some of the puzzles are sorely lacking in direction.  One example of this is some puzzles where you find zodiac symbols painted somewhere and some tokens.  You got the order the tokens go in, but then you also have to put some decorations into the right order as well, with absolutely no idea how they should go and each token has 4 different combinations multiplied by 4 tokens total, which makes for a lot of trial and error to actually solve the puzzle.
So overall, it's a good enough game, but some core gameplay elements will leave you frustrated and wanting to turn to a guide that at the time of writing this, doesn't seem to exist or at least my google skills are failing to find one.  The game runs fine, definitely doesn't have any bugs that I've found yet, the main issue is going to be how little direction you are given and how the hint system barely is of any help and that makes the game harder than it needs to be.

I'm going to list some of the pros and cons, so new players can get a general idea of what this game is about and the overall feeling of it all. This game has been in Early Access for a while, and yes, they're constantly updating it. For the time I've spent on it ( 30 hours over several months ) I seen tremendous improvement and balance efforts. The community can and usually does get suggestions to the devs, and they tend to listen. This is great and I'm sure many people enjoy the openness. One thing I feel the need to get across, is that this game is NOT Overwatch, Overwatch is more visually there while Paladins takes on an cartoon-istic approach. Paladins also has a wider range of champions, though some do seem to be Overwatch clones.
Pros to this Game :
-Cheap alternative to Overwatch with different features
-Lots of patches
-Fast paced gameplay
-Ranked doesn't have noobs
-Most Champions Are Cheap
-Weekly Champion Rotation
-Lots of chances to get cosmetics
-Immense amount of maps
-Sbility to vote on new maps
Cons to this Game :
-General lack of communication between players
-Toxic Community
-Plenty of players don't lock in
-Lots of bugs that don't get fixed
-Cosmetics tend to cost a lot
-Newer Champions drain your money for weeks
- Problems that I have found -
The sound bug, which hasn't been patched yet.
( Occurs when multiple players fight around each other )
The sound becomes loud and static-like and is your game might slow down.
How I've fixed it?
Your compatability might have to be adjusted and/or change your headphones while the game is open? Plenty of tutorials.
The Sudden Closing of the game during matches.
( No solution )
Overall I think this game could be polished, patched, and sold as a full-fledged game right now, and people would buy it. The people who claim that it's pay-to-win want a lot of the cosmetic items, which mean nothing to the actuall gameplay, and cards, which don't affect a person's skill level in the slightest. This game is free, which means it is giving you a lot for nothing. So stop complaining, and be happy with getting a game that could rival Overwatch with a few patches, for free.

First off, it's worth notig I am still reltively ne to the game, and that I am looking for something to replace RuneScape for me...which I've tried over 50 MMORPG games and nothing has really drawn me in yet. When it comes to Aura Kingdom thus far, it offers quite a bit but it also leaves somethings to be desired. The biggest issue for me is lack of GUI customization, I'm not one to really care abotu this...but when I can't even create a character because I'm using a 4K monitor and the 4K optimization is poor, it really doesn't leave a good impression. After about one hour of tweaking I was able to fix the issue (go into game files, disable high DPI scaling on the .exe launcher, not on the desktop shortcut) and get into the game, but then the GUI scale was limited to 130% which is not enough to make it easily viewable, I need 150-160% and it would be fine but for some reason they thought 130% would be okay. This isn't a game breaking issue, but it's one you shouldn't neglect this day in age...that's only going to show me you don't care enoguht o pay close attention to detail which makes me question what else you neglected. There is also one other big issue, that being the auto pathing, this is nice when I want to be lazy but it really destroys immersion. The last but least important issue is that you can skip dialogue, this is also going to ruin immersion and take away the storIf that wasn't bad enough, the sense of direction just isn't there so I feel forced to use it otherwise I have no clue where I'm going. There could be bigger issues, but I wish they wouldn't have opted for auto pathing, it's just not what a game should have. That's all of the bad I could really find in the game...the good, however, outweighs that tremendously. The combat is like a normal MMO, but it's got better flow and the abilities are far more interesting and diverse. You're going to want to figure out a rotation like you would in other MMOs, but it's not nearly as bland as some. Especially when you add the eidolons which are a really refeshing aspect. They're quite different from familiars/followers in the aspect they can be upgraded and have a special move, and there are a lot of them to choose from and they all have varying specializations and stats so you can choose the one that best suits your playstyle. If the abundant eidolons weren't enough, the abundant classes may be. There are so many different classes this should keep one entertained for quite some time. I couldn't decide at first, but ended up going with a wizard because I'm always drawn to the magical classes of all games. Overall, this is quite a different game, it's got its ups and downs but so far I do like it and it's keeping my attention for now so I would recommend it.

Screencheat is a crazy game about looking at the other players' screens to see where they are, and then proceeding to run them over with a toy horse, shoot them through a wall, blow them up with a teddy bear, or whack them to death with a fish.
As you can tell from the name, the videos and the screenshots, the game is splitscreen, and everyone is invisible. You have to locate the other players by screencheating, and then go and kill them. Every kill is satisfying. A ragdoll flops into existence when someone dies, and the ragdoll models include fish-people and chickens. There is an announcer, whose accent can be changed in the options. My personal favourite is the Australian announcer :D
There are 10 maps, which are well designed and colour-coded so that you can easily tell which area someone is in. There are 10 weapons, which are all unique. There are several different gamemodes, such as CTF (Capture the Fun), Deathmatch, KOTH, Murder Mystery (you are assigned a target that you must kill to gain points), and Juggernaut, to name a few. The gamemodes can be played FFA or in teams. There are also several server mutators which can be activated to create an even more hilarious/weird experience, like huge ragdolls, and Australian mode.
The game supports up to 8 players on a server. 4 players is a nice number, but a full server of 8 is pure insanity, and it's wonderful. You can play local or online multiplayer, or both at once.
You gain exp by playing, and as you level up you unlock bonus ragdolls (such as a hotdog) and weapon skins (such as the Cod of Duty skin for the melee weapon).
Overall it's a really fun game, and it's even more fun if you have friends to play with. It would probably be a great party game. There are so many funny moments, but it can be quite competitive too, and it gets pretty intense sometimes. But it's always fun! The game needs more people playing it, so buy it sometime!

Now within the game itself the board layout has also change, for newcomers probably intuitive enough, for those who have already spent quite a lot of time in the game a nuisance.
All of the things I've mentioned above are not the reason I can't recommend this game though.
The reason you should stay away until they patch this game: after you've finished a round the game just hangs with a white screen, no reaction at all, nothing. Couldn't even close it properly and had to kill it through the taskmanager. I'm definitely not willing to spend 5 minutes waiting for the game to load, navigate through submenus to pick a map and then have the game crash after one round.

This is a very hasty recommendation.
Doom or 'New Doom' as I'll call it, is an excellent shooter- one of the best on the market today as of Q2 2017.
It looks gorgeous and the gun audio is on point, everything looks and sounds even better than you'd expect.
Doom gets nothing wrong when it comes to shooting demons with every different kind of upgradeable weapon
you can think of- plus the glory kills are rad.
Saying that, going into this game I expected the glory kill system to get old quite quickly, yet it was the game itself which
did that for me. Glory kills switch up most of the time so you don't see the same repetitive animation too much, the developers understood this and made it a great compromise. Why didn't they understand that about the game itself?
DOOM is an excellent and mechanically brilliant FPS in a Groundhog Day style loop. Every mission is fairly similar
-cutscene
-shoot minions
-destroy gross demon thing which spawns boss demons
-destroy all demons
-progress
The only break in this rule tends to be when the game gives you a new weapon or sends you on an obligatory platforming mission which well and truly breaks whatever pace the game had left.
Overall, this is a great callback to the original DOOM- repetitive slaughter of demon after demon for self mastibatory satisfaction of the player.
John Romero, creator of DOOM once famously said that people did not buy video games for story or substance, simply for the experience of the game itself- something I profoundly disagree with, but if we adhere to his maxim 'New Doom' entirely fails in being a worthwhile experience. If you want to scratch that ID Software itch, maybe return to Wolfenstein the New Order or wait for Quake later down the line. However, if you're only interested in repetitvely shooting demons- this is the game for you.

If you're willing to put in the time to master this controller and set up configurations for the games you play, then it might be the best controller ever made outside of a mouse and keyboard. This is not a pick up and play device. You need to play around with what works and what doesn't work for you personally. After about 20 hours with this controller in CS:GO, I have a configuration that is absolutely perfect for me and I can play competively while lounging on my couch. Most community configurations are pretty solid so you just have to experiment.
I use a combination of the built in gyro and touch pad in most games to simulate the precision of a mouse and keyboard. Some games like Cities Skylines have pre-made developer configurations that work really well. I love this thing although I'll admit the learning curve is steep.
In conclusion, you'll get out of the Steam Controller what you put into it. If you're willing to figure out what works best for you then it works as advertised. I love the fact that I can play games like CS:GO, Dota 2 and other keyboard mouse intensive games while laying in my recliner in my living room and keep up with players using a mouse for precise movement. It's the ultimate tool for the lazy PC gamer, but only after you set it up for the games you play.
Pros:
-TouchPad gyro combo works super well, feels great
-Super long battery life
-Tons and tons of customization options for any genre
Cons:
-Takes time to wrap your head around it
-Can only be configured in Big Picture mode
-Some games take a long time to figure out a comfortable configuration

Dead Rising 3 is a third person zombie action game. I played the previous two games on Xbox 360 and while I wouldn't rate them among my favourite games, I did have some fun with them. I feel the same way about DR3. Its a decent game, but nothing special.
The player controls Nick Ramos, a mechanic who has been trapped along with a few other survivors, in the town of Los Perdidos, after a zombie outbreak. The government are planning to stop the outbreak by bombing the town, so you've got six days to find a way to escape.
Combat is primarily focused on melee, using whatever objects you can find lying around. Nick can also combine certain items together to create powerful combo weapons. For example the flaming sword will set zombies on fire, and the electrified sledgehammer will chain electricity damage to nearby zombies, so is great for fighting through a large crowd. The gun mechanics are weak, but thankfully you don't need to use them very often. Guns can be useful against living enemies (soldiers with guns, bikers with melee weapons) but melee works just fine too. You can use vehicles to drive around the town and run over zombies, and Nick can also create special combo vehicles.
As with previous games, you regain health by eating food that you find lying around the various buildings. You have a limited inventory so you need to decide how you split the space between melee, guns, crafting and food items. You can fight alone, in coop, or with AI controlled survivors. The AI is surprisingly capable, as long as you give them a decent weapon and keep an eye on their health, they won't die easily.
I was disappointed with the size of the map. The store page describes this as a "massive open world", which is simply not true. The last 3 games I've played before this were Shadow of Mordor, Dragon Age Inquisition and Far Cry 4. Those are "massive". DR3 is probably larger than the previous games in the series, but still quite small compared to most other open world games. It doesn't help that the town layout is four square zones connected by long roads, and then a large empty void in the middle, so alot of space is wasted. Missions take you to the same locations over and over and over again. I lost count of how many times I had to visit this one mansion in the north east to fight a different group of people.
The story is probably the best part of the game, because there's an interesting conspiracy going on. Since DR2, civilians have been getting implanted with chips containing Zombrex medicine which is supposed to prevent them from turning, so why isn't it working? Who started the outbreak? There are some unusual characters who continue the series tradition of wacky over the top humour.
DR3 also has problems from a technical point of view. The framerate is officially locked to 30 FPS, and just turning the camera felt uncomfortable. Thankfully you can unlock it (see the forum). I couldn't maintain 60 FPS because of the massive amount of zombies on screen, I was mostly bouncing around the 40's but that felt much more playable. However there are lots of other little things that aren't game breaking but they're just a bit annoying. Like how my weapons would clip through the body of an NPC that I'm talking to. Or the fact that after you go inside a building you CAN'T CLOSE THE DOOR to keep zombies out. Or if there are two items lying on the ground close to each other, its really tricky to highlight the one you actually want to pick up.
Overall DR3 can be enjoyable but its flaws prevent me from saying that its an essential purchase. If you're a series fan or you just like killing zombies, I'd suggest picking it up on a sale.

you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

is an unusual experiment that trades heavily on novelty but fails to leave a lasting impression.
The game presents itself as a tourist guidebook-esque visual novel intended for English-speaking audiences--this being rather alien territory for the genre--with all the trappings of the genre. Indeed, the attractive (albeit limited) art, interface and scenario design are rooted in the traditions of the Japanese visual novel. Unforunately, the experience is too brief and the informational aspect too slim; the game falls short of both of its propositions.
While the premise is intriguing, the characters are archetypal and the attempts at comedy and romance are tired and toneless. The main character--a foreigner homestaying with a pair of Japanese siblings--is merely a palette swap of the garden-variety protagonists found in lesser Japanese visual novels. His amorous leanings disappoint with their banal outcomes, and the girls fare no better. Makoto is a classical Japanese housewife-type whose prinicpal character flaw is an apparent inability to follow a recipe. Akira is a stand-offish, zesty younger sister whose conflicted romantic intentions toward the main character are too expected and textureless to muster any emotion in the player.
The game scenario branches into two storylines focusing on either girl, though the player receives no warning of how the limited choices to be made over the course of the game lead to which unaffecting outcome. The overall narrative has a distinct back-patting tone when mention is made of various technologies employed throughout Tokyo. The protagonist's constant amazement of Japanese technological progress and paradisiacal protrayal of Japanese life should strike any player familiar with the reality of living in Japan as disingenuous and irresponsible.
As a resource for would-be tourists, there is still more disappointment in store. The various guided tours of areas within Tokyo (and a few out-of-prefecture day trips) feel spartan and excessively-curated. Visits to points of interest within a given locale can be counted on one hand, and each day of the week's adventure ends before it seems to have begun. Wikipedia offers a more comprehensive study of the various neighborhoods of Tokyo than can be found in this game.
The game allows for currency conversions for all transactions in the game, ostensibly to fascilitate budgeting for a similar trip, but the usefulness of the feature is destroyed by how many costs are overlooked. That the protagonist lodges with a Japanese family--at no cost to him, one must presume--disregards one of the most significant expenses of a trip to Japan. Sadly, the greater preoccupation of the scenario writer was clearly the trite romantic comedy woven between the educational passages.
The music is servicable fare, limited to a handful of tunes that never become grating, if only due to the brevity of the game. Characters do not speak their lines, and aside from occasional sound effects, the background music is left to carry the scenes--a challenge far beyond its capacity.
A small offering of bonus features becomes availabe at the end of the first playthrough, though these provide little incentive to return to the shopworn storyline.
Fans of novelty and experimentation will find some redeeming qualities in what
has accomplished, but anyone looking for a captivating narrative or a useful resource for planning a stay in Japan would be better served by almost anything else.

After more than 70 hours, I'm finally done with this game... And what can I say about it ? I really really enjoyed it. This game DOES have an atmosphere. You really feel like you are in the wasteland, in this desert 2 centuries after the Great War that brought the end of the world.
Plus it's the kind of game where your choices actually matter, and change the way you play. You sometimes will be the one to decide wether you will save a village because you're a good guy, or we will blow it up, like the city of Gecko for example. Same for Vault 13, you can decide to help or... kill the inhabitants, it's up to you.
But there's one thing I can blame this game for: it is not well balanced. By this I mean you will sometimes have to face very strong ennemies (especially during random encounters) while you are still low level. But once you get the power armor, you are almost invincible because most ennemies won't even be able to hurt you.
So yes, I strongly recommand Fallout 2 even if you may turn crazy because it tends to be kinda hard sometimes. But you will enjoy it because of the combat system and the atmosphere. It's light years away from Fallout 4...

It's not often that I put together any sort of cohesive thoughts in any of my reviews, instead resorting to a "GOOD OR BAD," similar to the way CNN runs the news.
After playing this game for 22 straight hours, I can say that it comes highly reccomended as one of the best games in the past 10 years. Rock solid gameplay mechanics, deep progression and customization options, and a plethora of items and gameplay styles to suit any player.
The game is definitely my favorite narrative experience in a game in the past year, and I could probably rank it in the leagues of Half-Life 2. It's an incredible experience with rich characters. The amount of flexibility in the conversation system is pretty great and the voice acting is sufficient (though not stellar) and moves the story along just fine.
So yes, I definitely reccomend this game to anyone who likes a good shooter, or a good stealth game, or any game with a good narrative. Really, unless you spend your days playing Reader Rabbit and Freddi Fish, you need to play this game.

I'm tempted to give this a thumbs down, not because of the game itself - but because the Director's Cut is of... dubious quality.  It does improve the boss fights a little, making them a little more flexible so that you won't be torn a new ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if you choose to make a stealthy character build.  There are also a few small graphical fixes and all the DLC content such as a mission available with pre-orders and the MissingLink chapter are included and streamlined into the game.  But bugs are bugs are bugs, and this version of the game is MUCH buggier.  Still.. it's relatively cheap and they have offered a discount for owners of the base game, and if you can forgive the fact that this version occasionally bugs out more - it's still a damned great game and it is nice to have certain features added in and to be able to play The Missing Link chapters with your character build and for experience gained there to add to that build, something that was unavailable before (Though they did give you the ability to add some augments at the beginning of Missing Link so it wouldn't be totally unfair.)  and while the Boss fights are still a low point, they are handled a little better here.
It helps that the base game is superb.  While not as good as the original Deus Ex, it DID manage to capture the feel of the game and even some of its depth without dumbing it down to the level that the disappointing Invisible War did; and while Invisible War is still a decent game, Human Revolution is a much better successor and I will admit that if there is one area that Human Revolution exceeds the original is in its story, which is much more personal, and brings in some well handled philosophical elements.  I also love the games art design which is best described as a mixture of the luminous amber world and antequated but nonetheless stylish fashion of Mamoru Oshii's excellent animated film "Innocence" and the bleak cyberpunk hodgepodge from Ridley Scott's legendary "Blade Runner."  While the graphics are admittedly fairly dated, particularly in regards to some ugly as sin chararcter models and animations, it makes up for it with this attractive art design and does at least have some incredible lighting work.  The game is actually very atmospheric despite somewhat simplistic hub world design, and it's easy to get sucked in the hubs, even if the load times are a bit frequent and lengthy.  I especially love the Shanghai hub, it was my favourite hub in Deus Ex 1 as well - it appealed to me greatly because I love the idea of mixing Cyberpunk, the Shanghai Night Life, and Triads!  Can't go wrong with Triads.  Well, you could and they might mess you up... but whatever, they're still cool.
The game is also fairly replayable, maybe not to the same extent as the original Deus Ex but still to an extent that many modern single player games simply don't offer.  It helps that your characters build affects the way the game plays; the game could be a tactical cover based shooter if you like.  Or it can be a Metal Gear Solid-esque stealth 'em up (My favourite route) or if you are good enough, a brutal but challenging FPS.  If you haven't played this yet - give this version a chance!  If you have played this before, really consider whether or not you feel if the more complete experience is worth some of the bugs and problems with this release.  Some people may just prefer to re-install the original edition, but others - myself included - may appreciate the more complete experience and can get over some of the oddities.

Note: This review was written on 20160906, but could not be posted due to Steam Store Page issues with the game. I've not updated the review since then.
Skara - The Blade Remains is an online multiplayer arena fighting game with a fantasy gladiator setting. It's currently in Early Access, but I believe it's very close to release.
There's some lore around the character races and setting, but ultimately it's fairly irrelevant to the gameplay, which involves beating opponents to a pulp in short- to medium-length arena combat.
Graphics in Skara are a bit of a mixed bag. The character graphics and animations are quite good, and the team deathmatch arena looks quite impressive, but the other two arenas and the various special effects are a bit of a letdown.
I also noticed heavy motion blur when turning, which both looks a bit meh and also slows down the game noticeably on my gaming laptop (admittedly a fairly old one). Unfortunately there seems to be no way to turn this effect off without lowering the overall graphics detail, as there's only one variable setting available for graphics quality.
Skara features fairly typical gladiatorial type battle music, which fits the game well. It's nothing I'd want to listen to outside of the game, but I didn't see any need to turn it off or adjust the volume down.
Sound effects, too, are suitable, if nothing out of the ordinary for the genre.
When you begin Skara you're given a single character slot and a choice of three races to choose from, each with names that you'll not remember or be able to pronounce unless you're familiar with the world. There's no customisation available unless you use real money to purchase gems to customise your armour, helmet, or weapons, but the developers were wise enough to make these cosmetic only, rather than falling down the pay-to-win rabbit hole. But it does mean that basically all characters of each race look the same, so you'll quickly become used to recognising what's what.
There's a brief tutorial that introduces you to the basic moves. Full controller support is available, so I played with an Xbox controller, which worked fine: left stick for movement, right for targeting; triggers for block and basic attacks, B for dodge, and A/X/Y for race-specific attacks, one of which is ranged for each race.
The game then drops you on the main screen, from which you can choose to fight in one of three arenas: duel (one on one), free for all (four players, the most kills wins), and team deathmatch (four vs four, a sort of 'hold the fort' type of arena). The most fun and interesting of these by far was the team deathmatch arena, which is well designed and very pretty. The free-for-all arena is reasonable, too, with a trapped area that can be sprung by any player and a 'boss' fighter that is released towards the end to change it up a bit. The one-on-one duels are the most disappointing, and the arena is small and not much fun, with obstacles constantly blocking you in when you try to manoeuvre.
Regardless of mode, the game uses an automatic third-person 3D camera that mostly keeps up with action well. I did find myself off camera a few times, and fell to my death multiple times in each arena due to the camera focusing on my targeted enemy and making it hard to keep track of the level dangers.
Unfortunately, though, the online-only nature of Skara means that even with a relatively good ADSL2 connection I found the lag unbearable at times. I'd press my assassin character's 'blink' attack button, watch her shoot across the screen and then the game would catch up, teleport her backwards, and drop her right in front of my enemy's swinging blade. Countless times I'd be mid-attack and my target would disappear and reappear out of range behind me somewhere. Even against bots the network code just doesn't seem to cope well enough for an action game like this, where timing is everything.
Skara includes character progression through gold and experience points. The former can be used to buy extra abilities, of which there are only very few available, while increases in the latter improves your account level (which is the same across all of your characters), which unlocks extra slots in the game as you progress, giving you space for up to three characters with multiple ability slots. It's a good idea, but as with the game as a whole, it's only fairly limited in scope.
Remembering that Skara is still in Early Access, I don't want to be too harsh on it. But something really does need to be done to improve the networking, as lag is a killer in a game like this. Load times, too, are incredibly long; I waited 28 seconds (in-game counter) just for the main screen to disappear after selecting a battle arena type, and then it took about the same time again for the actual lobby to load. Other minor issues include the use of Steam name in some places, even after asking for a different screen name, and terrible grammar in some places. I'm not sure whether the game will include more arena and character variety after release, but I hope so; the choices at the moment are fairly limited.
Pros:
+ Fairly good character graphics and animations
+ Team deathmatch arena is very pretty, and the game mode is fun
+ Free for all arena is interesting and original
+ Progression system is a good idea and a good start
+ Trading Cards (although as with other F2P games I assume these won't drop after release if you get the game for free)
Cons:
- Lag makes the 'timing, precision and accuracy' required for intelligent play almost impossible
- Very long loading times
- It's very easy to fall to your death on any of the arenas
- Only three arenas, one of which (ice lake) is rather poor indeed
- Limited character selection and customisation (only through purchased gems)
- Limited progression limits replayability
- Motion blur is annoying
- Other minor EA issues (e.g. poor grammar, Steam name used sometimes rather than screen name)
Skara - The Blade Remains is very hard to not recommend now that it's relatively easily obtainable for free, and will soon be released as free-to-play on Steam. It has its problems, but even when you can't find anyone online it's still fun beating up the bots for a few hours. With more arenas and characters, better loading times, and a big reduction in lag, it would be much better, though.

This is an updated review.
First of all, if you are looking for a quality, multiplayer (over the internet) board game with easy to understand concepts, this is it. It's a game witha great reputation as a traditional board game, but it really does well as a PC game. And incidentally, I also own this title and all the DLC for my iPad as well (and it's even a more perfect fit as an electronic game on that platform).
It's easy to understand how to play this game and the interface works perfectly as an electronic game.
Ticket to Ride relies a lot on skill and critical thinking and some on chance. A more advanced player definitely has the capability to make the game more complex for the opponent.  The single player vs one AI is not very challenging, but that's OK. It's still a fun diversion.
I did have an issue a while back that had me giving this game a thumbs down. It was because my game was broken and nothing I did would fix it (for a while). Support tried to help me, but they were slow between communications, and never came up with an answer. Frankly, I'm not sure how they ever would, considering the weird nature of the issue.
Finally I was able to resolve the issue, by accident.
The issue was I could not get a single player versus one AI to load the game board so the game would not start. I solved it accidentally by loading up a single player versus TWO AI, then I backed out, tried with one AI, and it loaded. I have repeated this solution several times.  If you are having that issue, might want to give that a try. /shrugs
Anyway, with the issue solved and enjoying many games with my friend - online - and as a single player against AI (once again), I do not regret this purchase, and thereby change my review to a resounding "Yes!"
I mostly only play against AI, but this is a solid adaptation of the board game. I definitely recommend it if you've ever found yourself pining for a game while stuck at your desk :p

The original changed my life back in 94. It got me into modding which eventually led me to software engineering. It's difficult for me to be objective about DOOM but I'll try.
This 2016 remake is a worthy successor in the series. It takes the strengths of the original (spooky atmosphere, rooms full of demons, power fantasy) and wraps them in a beautiful engine with modern gameplay traits. These modern traits, like a progression system, FPS movement changes, never feel tacked on mind you. Instead they add extra depth we've come to expect nowadays.
The campaign is not overly long but the skill challenges and (with a later patch) the arcade mode give you plenty to do. The story is pulpy as you'd want in a DOOM game. The characters take themselves seriously but the protagonist goes through it as we, as players, should: fast and unconcerned.
A true come back from id Software, focusing on gameplay while not losing sight of a beautiful presentation.

The premise is simple, yet very well executed: You're alone trying to survive and escape the tundra with whatever items you can find at an abandoned base, your only guidance and communication from the outside world is via teletype. This game is proof you don't need much to create a tense and immersive survival experience.

Note:
Those are the two words that I would use to describe my experience playing the game “Near Death”. To survive you must have a purpose for task at hand and do so with urgency. Every second spent out in the open away from a source of heat brings you another moment closer to death.
There is no need for large animals or scary monsters hunting you when the wind and the dropping temperature of the air you breath can kill you just as fast! As the game progresses the intensity of the wind literally pushes your player character around the environment as you struggle from one location to the next.
“Near Death” has great atmosphere and soundtrack. There is basic crafting and inventory management. It also forces you to read a map and the terrain. As with real life, before GPS on every phone anyway, there is no blinking dot on the map to tell you where you are.  It can be easy to get lost in the near white out conditions and perish.
The only downside to this game is the relatively short time it takes to complete. Although, I say it is a short game I don’t mean it to sound like I feel cheated in any way. There is a story to follow and a mission to complete. Extending the story any longer would have detracted from the Urgency that you feel while playing.
Was it worth the cost of the game? For myself, who purchased the game during a Steam Winter sale the answer is absolutely. Is it worth the full $15? That would be harder to say. Would I still have enjoyed it as much? Without a doubt! If you aren’t convinced pick it up during the next sale.

This game is quite the oddity, the issue I see here is that a lot of people havent seemed to understand who it is meant to be for, who they are aiming it for. This is more casual and"we are going on an adventure" 4/5 years ago back when we minecraft was taking off that was the whole point of it, going on an adventure, this is sort what that is about but more dramatic. If you are in this expecting some break neck emotions and and certain death then think again.
One would expect that the the casual nature would cause issues but it doesnt, there is a very small amount of cheese and the overarching storyline grips you enough to want to smash though it, there is the issue however that the decisions you face isnt as large, you arent dooming someone to death if they leave the party for example. As for the length I think its just about right for what it is meant to be, its around 8 hours long and I finished it in two sittings, could have done it in one and wanted to but I need sleep.
Few issues as there is dlc for three more chapters adding around 3-4hours of content from what I understand but the ending is done in a way where that isnt too much of an issue and it can easily stand on its own without the dlc added on.
Just understand this isnt some brutal horrors of war sort of game, its lighthearted and it comes in a nice place when you consider how many gritty games there are these days so if you are looking to chill out for a little while this seems like a great game to grab and its a steal if you can get it on a sale.

I got this controller as a Christmas present and it has been a complete surprise for me. For years I have used the xbox360 controller to play games, so at first the steam controller was very foreign to me. However, after a month's use I can not play games without it.
The controller itself is very cheaply built and when you first get it, it will seem underwhelming, but the functions and capabilities of the controller far outweigh its poor build quality. The touchpad is fantastic after you get used to it, and I can definitely see it becoming the new "thing" for controllers to have. Also, the buttons behind the grips are also very useful and work well in games where you might have to modify the controller to work with the game.
Speaking of modifying the controller, this is now easier than ever! Games that don't support the steam controller allow for you to set your own configurations which can be made exactly the way you want them. Additionally, you can just upload anybody elses configuration and use it. This customization makes the steam controller a huge draw for anyone.
One of the things that I think is very understated for controllers these days are their battery life, and the steam controller's is excellent. Although it does not take a battery pack (just AA batteries) I have gotten a ton of life out of the controller and have not replaced the batteries once. This is a far cry from changing the battery packs on my old xbox controllers every few hours.
Build Quality- 4/10
Functions/Capabilities- 9/10
Customization- 9/10
Battery Life- 9/10
Overall this is a great controller and I recommend it to anyone who plays a lot of games with a controller.

it's without a doubt the most interesting controller i've used but even after trying numerous community profiles and my own custom profiles with several different games i can't find a way of using it that feels natural (and i've been using it for around a month).
turning the thing off is a hassle.  why doesn't it have an option to just shut off automatically when you exit big picture mode?  right now you have to press the steam button to go into big picture mode, hold the button to access a menu to turn off the controller, and then use your keyboard and mouse to exit big picture mode.  what the actual hell were they thinking with this?  you could use their whole battery ejecting mechanism inside of the controller but the back of the controller you have to remove to access this is a flimsy curved piece of plastic.
ergonomically it's doing something extremely wrong because the tendons in my thumbs are in absolute AGONY after about 30 mins of playing a FPS with the controller.  this is easily the most offending part about it and i can't recommend it in its current state because of this.  it's hard to get used to the controller if my hands are in excruciating pain after barely using it in one sitting.
the haptic feedback is cool and i couldn't imagine not having it with this kind of controller---it was a smart decision----but this means no more rumble.  i tried playing sonic racing transformed and i couldn't even drift properly.  it's a weird experience playing games you are used to playing with rumble.  dunno if that's a good thing or not.
maybe in a few hardware revisions it'll be better.  i don't really see why you'd burden yourself trying to play games like baldur's gate with this instead of with a keyboard and mouse, but hey--more power to you!  unless you are interested in doing a gyroscope and touchpad approach for your FPS controls you are not going to be happy with it for shooters either---i had a lot of trouble using this for a game like portal and couldn't get it to feel right no matter which profile i used.  i ended up spending loads more time setting up the controller instead of actually playing games with it and i think that's the biggest problem with it in its current state: unless you have the time to fuss around with your controller and figure out what feels right you would probably be better served with an xbox 360 controller.  at least that won't have you experiencing excruciating pain after 30 minutes of playing a shooter with it.
There is, at least for me, a bit of a learning curve if you're used to using an analog stick on the right. But otherwise its a good controller and its very verstile.

After almost two months with this controller I can say that I would recommend it (with some exceptions).
The start was really awkward and definitelly not what I expected. None of the games were easy to control. And thats also with those with official controller support. A day later, a firmware update made most of the problems disappear and it became actually usable.
It still took some time to get used to it, but now I prefer this over my old XBOX style gamepad. There are lots of ways to configure controller for almost every game. Haptic feedback creates a feeling of having physical controlls for the gamepads. Mouse-like aiming is definitelly more accurate that usual left-stick aim + can be even more accurate if gyroscope is used for precission.
I also tried using gyro as a wheel in racing games, but that didn't work very well. A way to bind a key to open on-screen keyboard (which is surprisingly usable) would be nice. Battery life seems to be great - the original batteries still work fine. Controller can also be used with a cable. Sadly, batteries don't recharge.
Even though I like this gamepad, I definitelly wouldn't recommend this to anyone who has a "gaming corner" and never plays from a couch or hates "Big Screen". This device is great for couch gaming, but does nothing that mouse + keyboard wouldn't do better.

When I started pc gaming, I wanted more ways to do things besides keyboard and mouse. I was tired of games not having support or changeable configurations. Why is it that I can choose what 'A' does on my keyboard, but not my controller? After searching and finding many failures, I found the steam controller.
I immediately dove into the world of customization, comfort, and individuality that is the realm of the steam controller. My favourite part about it is that I can set it up ANY way I want. The grips work perfect, I love the dual-stage triggers, the way that the pads rumble is exciting, and the gyroscope functionality just blew my mind! I really love how VALVe took notice of the workshop and allows you to use community configurations to save you time and effort. The only downsides to the controller are ones that should be fixed with updates.
As a whole, I see little-to-no downsides with this amazing piece of hardware and actually wish I had more than one! I recommend it to anybody that is familiar with a controller or keyboard and needs a way to play and relax.

I played a bit of Aura Kingdom during my WoW downtime. Thought I'd give a brief review of my experience.
Played I would say for the last two weeks very casually. The game has an auto pathing system that take a lot of the running around(exploring) out of the game. I actually liked the system because it let's you pickup and play easily without having to really invest. It also got me to actually pay attention to the story not that is was mind blowing.
The art is the games strongest point. It sort of reminds of the "Tales of" series. The costumes are also suuppperrr on point. Very cute, or very cool mounts, and Edilons(your fighting companion pets). The world isnt too bad and some of creature you fight are cool looking as well.
The class system I didn't get to fully explore. I rolled a Bard which is the games only pure healing class. It can still easily solo from what I saw and I had a few duels with other players winning with superior healing. At level 40 they let you choose from any of sub classes, three of which offer additonal spells with the right off hand weapon equipped. The system allows for some super creative ways to play but ultimately some are clearly better than others as MMORPG's go.
The community however is dead. Like there are people EVERYWHERE, but we can't talk. My entire time I spoke to no other players. You have to purchase an item from the store just to talk in /world chat and it has only so many uses. You may end up paying for an item just to have your message spammed out of sight. I was invited to a guild, no one was ever on. I never found a group for running dungeons either...
The cash shop wasn't too bad. I purchaes 2500 Aeria Points for about 32$ CAN and got a very cool costume for my character, and some large 20 slot bags. They also give you a bunch of items with EXP and Drop rate buffs, and a free mount. Later on I found out that I get even more free stuff which was x3 more 20 slot bags, and two more Edilon pets one of which is worth 50.00$ in the cash shop.
I found this game to be actually quite enjoyable. If I wasn't looking forward more so to WoW Legion I might consider giving it more time. I've never been a fan of "Pay to Win" but I am a fan of seeing how far you can take a free to play character. Even so the cash shop has some fair deals and most of the items in there are cosmetic in nature from what I saw.
Do you like MMORPG's? Do you like Anime? Then you might like Aura Kingdom

I believe this isn't my first review, although it certainly feels like it. Please forgive me if the following review is somewhat disjointed or disorganized in its structure. I would also like to tell you to take both my review and other reviews of this (and any game) with a pinch of salt. What I've written here are, of course, my own opinions. If this game interests you at all after reading this review, you should try it and form your own opinion on it!
is a multiplayer online team-based battle arena (or perhaps I should call it a fighting game?) with controls and gameplay similar to that of Lords of the Fallen or Dark Souls. You could call it a MOBA with the exceptions of the usual towers and minions that are commonly associated with those kind of games - this is all about the fighting. It is being developed by an independant group (in Spain if I'm not mistaken). It is currently in open alpha testing at the time of this review.
To be perfectly honest, I went into this game with a clean mind. I had read many of the negative (and positive) reviews and so I decided it would be better to form my own opinion. I was quite surprised by the game, though.
Skara has a lot of good elements going for it. While it is not
uncommon to find a third-person MOBA today, I think Skara is one of the only ones that actually has all of its emphasis on the fighting. If you've played a Souls game or something like Dragon's Dogma, you'll get the controls down pretty quickly. Other than your usual WASD-movement controls, your player character has a normal attack and a special attack which they can freely mix into combo attacks. Your character also has a defensive move (for instance, one character can block and another one can counter an attack with the right timing) and the ability to dodge (rolling, stepping or dashing depending on character) which gives you some frames of invincibility. It gives you all the tools necessary for enjoyable (if not a little clunky) intensive fights.
Apart from your basic moves, each of the character types have access to three "Signs", or abilities, unique to them. These can be all from throwing your shield while setting it on fire like a pyromaniac Captain America, or placing a trap that encases your enemy (or even yourself or your allies!) in ice so they can't move. These Signs add a lot of versatility to your character and really opens up for interesting tactics, especially during group fights.
Skara has two game modes currently, with a third one planned for release soon: A 1v1 duel mode and a 3v3 last man standing mode. The third game mode coming out is a 5v5 domination mode. I actually found it very interesting for a game like this to include a duel mode to begin with, and as such it was the first mode I ever played.
The biggest thing that Skara has going for it is how player-driven its development is. Players can post their suggestions and ideas for lore and even character designs and game features, and it is very important that they do so as well. A major part of how the game is played today is because of the feedback the game has received since the beginning of its development. At the time of writing this review, the developers are quickly and happily responding to queries and suggestions on the Steam discussion forums all the time, which is quite impressive.
Another large part of Skara is its lore, which does take the player-driven development into account. The previous highest-ranking players were placed as part of the game's lore, for instance. There's a lot to read and a lot to add to the lore, and I don't want to spoil it for you in case you decide to try the game out for yourself, so I think that's all I'll write about it.
The game currently has a shop where you can pay real currency to buy cosmetics (and only cosmetics, no pay to win here) for the different characters. The reason I bring this up in this section is because, at least in my opinion, the majority of the cosmetics look
! I've already spent some money on pimping out my two favorite characters! The graphics overall look very nice and really portrays the overall kind of grim atmosphere.
It really depends on your own tastes. As I mentioned, at the time of this writing the game is in open alpha, so there is a lack of content. The duel mode has one map, a frozen little island in the middle of the sea, and the last mand standing mode also only has one map, the lava coliseum. Currently, there are only 4 (with a 5th in the "Coming Soon-making) character types to play with, and even while they are very different from each other, there are indeed only 4.
There are bugs, of course. When me and a friend tried to add each other to our friends list or party the first time, it just didn't work - we had to restart the game first. Ever since it
worked though, and when I posted about it on the forums I got a quick reply from one of the developers too. The game is also not very optimized, which is a common thing for an early build, but still might put you off a little if you aren't expecting it. It doesn't slow down dramatically or anything like that, but it can have the occasional stuttering.
The matchmaking also seems a bit weird. Even though me and my friend queued up for dueling at the same time, it took the game ~40 seconds of searching for a match before we got to play. It's not a long time, but it is quite strange that it works like that. If you queue up and the game can't find another player, it will pit you against bots until a player takes its/their place.
On a final note, I do wish there were more diverse sound effects in the game. The ones that are in are not bad or stock by any means, but how the sound of a spear blade penetrating your flesh is the same sound as a massive pick made out of bone or a curved sword in eastern style is beyond me! It's not gamebreaking though and I imagine this is something that will change as the game develops further.
is a fun game. Fighting other players, especially in last man standing, is a blast and every fight feels different. It is not a perfect game as it lacks content (it is in alpha, after all) but the content it currently has is quite enjoyable. It has been said many times before, but this game has a lot of good potential (and so far it is not being wasted one bit). The only thing Skara really suffers from is a lack of players, and I can't stress that enough - if the game had more active players, it would likely be the one of the games I've invested the most hours in ever on my steam account, haha.

Skara - The Blade Remains is the newest audition in the competetive play gaming genre introducing unique styled combat and match system, with a lot of story behind every single character the game offers players to try. Although opinions for the game are mixed, the game is still in early phase of development, and for the early stages it is in, the developers have done a lot.
The combat style of the game is very unique and distinctive. Each character has 3 special abilities, and two default abilities - strong and normal strike. Strategical thinking and outsmarting the enemy is sometimes essential, because not only your survival and combat skills matter. The game has rich environment interaction, and it allows you trick players into traps leading you to victory. If your enemies are not careful enough, you wouldn't need to engage in combat, and just use the environment to your advantage.
Speaking of combat, the game allows players to free run, or lock on targets. Locking on targets is a must for best precision. Sometimes locking on targets unlocks passive abilities - like fast dashing, or running jump spear strike. Some characters have passive abilities, like shield defense.
Dive into this clash combat adventure in 1v1, 3v3 or 5v5 modes, each one on a different map, with different environmental rules. Discover the current and new incoming characters, and claim to become the best warrior of your faction in Skara - The Blade Remains.

This game has potential to be a competator for unturned, but there are so many bugs and polishing issues I cannot reccomend it. Even though it has been in 2 years of development
(Over Unturned)
-Bullet drop system
Holy Moly the bullet drop system is so nice! I wish Unturned had something like it. Unturned's bullet drop system works on the bullet constantly dropping down at the same rate, it never travels straight like a real bullet and then begins to start falling more and more. Nomad's bullet drop makes ranged shooting with a scope an ease. Like real life, the bullet travels straight for a split second, then gravity slowly starts increasing the drop. I wish unturned had something like this, but it does not.
-More detail on characters
Unturned's characters looks like a mannequin with no detail with no clothes on. In Nomad, you can actually see some details like belly button, knees, etc. Nothing really pervy, the nipples on the females are magically covered with their hair, yay for censorship?.
-Spawn Rates
This can be seen either as a pro or a con. The spawn rates are high enough to make it not too hard to find food/guns/tools for players. But not too high to make it seem like they are common. Unturned purposely makes it hard to find items because its realistic, you have to survive, not thrive.
(What Unturned is better at)
-Zombies' spawn rates
A zombie survival game has to have zombies, Where the heck are they? I cannot find any wherever I looked.
-Gun Models and Art style
Some of models of the guns and rest of the items are not up with this game's artstyle, its like the creator just took a bunch of models from other people and mashed them together in this game. Some guns like the Storm (AR-15) fit the style. While other guns like the magnum look like a cardboard cutout. Also, the reload animation of guns are so basic, there isn't even a animation for the charging handle, only putting a magazine in. Not to mention some sights are so low detailed you are better off aiming without them
-Network
The hit registration and network optimization is terrible. I connected to a US West server and was welcomed with a message saying I have over 300 ping. Hit registration isn't any better as it takes about 10-15 rounds to kill someone with a storm.
-Polishing
The animations are clunky and barebones. I mentioned that with the firearms, All the animations are the same for eating and drinking. Also the interface takes a second to pop up in my inventory, I also have to exit and go back into my inventory when I pickup something so I can interact with it.
-Being Bugfree
Ugh bugs, every gamer's worst nightmare, this game has a few of them. The worst one I know of is rarely when you exit your inventory, your character cannot move. Also the game studders when entering some areas. Nothing too bad, but you will notice some down the line.
TD:DR Unturned is better at almost everything except for this game's bullet drop system and character detail.

Fallout 2: A Post Nuclear Role Playing Game is a role-playing open world game featuring a considerably larger map/world and a far more extensive storyline, than those of Fallout 1.
It is hands down one of the best games I've ever played (and that says a lot about it). The fact that the game was made in 1998 makes it even more impressive.
Fallout 2 centres around the protagonist a.k.a. 'The Chosen One' and is entasked with the duty by the elder of his village to find and retrieve the Garden Eden Creation Kit (G.E.C.K.) which is a device that can create thriving communities out of the post-apocalyptic wasteland.
The game comprises of exploring and travelling in the open world as well as speech and quests to various characters and NPC. In addition to the role playing elements, a unique turn-based shooter is used during combat. This incredible blend  makes the game so widely stimulating and intense. It is an experience unlike one other. Not to mention the storyline is as engaging as it is compelling.
The player's actions throughout the game dictate what future story or gameplay opportunities are available. A player can choose to inhibit/aid certain NPCs and affects the entire gameplay. Aside from combat, speech also plays a huge role in the final outcome of the game.
Before the game begins, the player is allowed to create his/her character with a variety of different skill, perk, trait and character point (S.P.E.C.I.A.L) builds. Because of the extensive outcome and scenarios, Fallout 2 is a game with incredibly high replay value.
